  console created FOR us - `CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE`, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, an Explorer
  double-click - holds exactly one process. That distinction is what keeps every
  GUI launch in this suite non-CLI, which `new-window-cwd.ps1` A5/A6 depend on.
- **No console at all, but a console-owning parent**
  (`AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)`, released immediately). This is the
  release-build leg, and it is not academic: MSYS/git-bash resolves `ghoztty` to
  `ghoztty.exe`, since its transparent-extension magic covers `.exe` and not
  `.com`.

Two shared-core edits ride along, both Windows-guarded so POSIX is byte-for-byte
unchanged. The CLI default resolves to an **explicit cwd path**, not `.inherit`:
`.inherit` reports `value() == null`, and a null working directory on an agent
OPEN does not mean "the app's cwd", it means the AGENT's - `C:\Windows\System32`
for the one the HKCU Run entry starts - which is precisely the defect T144
fixed. And the `$SHELL` lookup stays off on Windows, because `SHELL` there is an
MSYS artifact holding `/usr/bin/bash`, which the win32 spawn cannot execute;
without that guard, a Ghoztty launched from a git-bash prompt would have come up
with every pane trying to run a POSIX path.

New acceptance script `test\win32\cli-launch-cwd.ps1` (ALL PASS) exercises all
four shapes on the box - the twin, the negative control, a shared console, and a
detached spawn from a console-owning parent - plus an arm that types
`echo T506MARK=[%GHOZTTY_CLI_LAUNCH%]` into the pane and reads it back, so the
marker's clearing is measured rather than assumed. That arm was teeth-checked by
making `clearMarker` a no-op and rebuilding: it went red and nothing else moved.
`auto-launch-cwd.ps1`, `new-window-cwd.ps1` and P1-P3 stay ALL PASS; all three
zig lanes pass.

One thing the validation turned up that is not ours: `persistence-flag.ps1` is
red with `undeclared: 4 of 169`, in `agent-attach-refused.ps1` and
`url-scheme.ps1` - files T506 never touched. Filed as **T744**.

- 2026-08-11: T533 - dragging a split divider now moves ONLY that divider. The user's report (2026-08-06, right after T495: "resizing the 1st sizer moves the 2nd sizer... I expect only the 2 panels being sized are [affected]") was drag SEMANTICS, not the drag MAPPING T495 fixed: the root ratio is the boundary between the first pane and the whole right SUBTREE, so leaving the nested ratio alone made the second divider slide by half of whatever the first one travelled and quietly shrank the far pane. New pure `src/apprt/win32/split_resize.zig` - sibling to `split_geometry.zig`, which says where the dragged divider goes while this says what the rest of the tree does about it. `plan()` returns the dragged node's ratio plus the compensating ratios that put every other same-axis boundary back on its pre-drag pixel; it recurses (a four-column run behaves like the three-column case at every level), walks THROUGH a perpendicular split rather than around it (a vertical divider is no boundary on the horizontal axis, but both of its children live in the range that changed - so a grid does not shear), and prunes any subtree whose axis range is unchanged, which leaves the other side bit-identical. Two details are the difference between working and nearly working: every tick re-solves from a PRE-DRAG snapshot rather than from the previous tick (ratios are `f16` and `axis` truncates, so "hold it where it is now" drifts over a few hundred motion ticks - and solving from the original also makes a drag exactly reversible), and the held ratio aims at the CENTER of its target pixel, since aiming at the edge lands a pixel low every time anything rounds down. A squeeze that cannot be honored gives way at the same [0.1, 0.9] band a dragged divider obeys, and the walk continues against the geometry that actually resulted. `Window.zig` snapshots the tab's tree into a fixed 128-node buffer at `startDividerDrag` (no allocation on the message loop) and re-validates it each tick; a tree too big, a divider whose region will not resolve, or a tree rebuilt mid-drag all fall back to the pre-T533 single-node resize rather than to a wrong one. 13 unit tests in the none lane, geometry swept at 1.0/1.25/1.5/2.0, including the defect itself as a control. `test\win32\split-divider.ps1` ALL PASS (62): a +-120px drag of the first divider leaves the second reading 1064 -> 1064, with a control arm proving the first one really tracked - teeth-checked by forcing the compensation off and rebuilding, where those arms go red (54px of slide, far pane 147 -> 93). Floor: none/win32/agent PASS, P1-P3 ALL PASS. Mac checked and does NOT compensate either (`SplitView.swift` binds each nested split to its own geometry), so this is a deliberate divergence rather than a parity port; the Mac half is filed as T754.

- 2026-08-11: T528 - the close button's X is WHITE on its red hover again, on every theme. The user's report (2026-08-06: "the close X button in the top right has black X on hover while normal windows have white X") was two correct rules producing one wrong button: `resolve` lifted `#C42B1C` to clear 3:1 off the band and then let `contrastForeground` pick the foreground, and on a mid-dark band (`#202020` -> bar `#323232`, luminance .032) the lift lands the red at luminance ~.196, where BLACK is the WCAG-correct answer at 4.91:1 and white only manages 4.27:1. Every floor passed; the button looked broken. The fix constrains the FILL rather than the foreground, which is the general rule where a convention names the foreground: `chrome_theme.dangerFillOn` caps the red's luminance at `1.05/4.5 - 0.05` so white always clears 4.5:1, and `on_danger` is white, full stop. The palette also stopped answering two questions with one color - `danger` is now the FILL (caption close hover, the connection pill's Reconnect capsule) and the new `danger_ink` is the MARK on the band (the tab strip's close glyph), which keeps the 3:1 chrome floor it always had and would have been dimmed by the cap. New primitive `color_math.cappedLuminance` searches CIELAB lightness down against the QUANTIZED color, so the 8-bit value it returns is itself under the ceiling. `remote_pill.ink` takes `pal.on_danger` instead of re-searching per state, and firms its fill DARKER on hover/press the way the caption slab already did. Where the cap and the 3:1 lift cannot both hold (bands around `#2F2F2F`..`#595959`) the convention wins and the fill sits at the cap - the sweeps assert that disjunction rather than dropping the floor. New `test\win32\close-glyph-white.ps1` (ALL PASS, 5) launches on `--background=#202020` deliberately, because on `caption-bar.ps1`'s `#000000` the old code picked white too and the arm would have passed against the defect; teeth-checked by restoring the searched foreground and rebuilding, where it reports a black X (darkest glyph pixel luminance 0.0) and goes 2 red. Design system §2.3 gained the rule. Floor: none/win32/agent PASS, P1-P3 ALL PASS, caption-bar/chrome-theme/remote-pill/tab-strip ALL PASS. Filed T755 (a `+list` sat blocked for 34 minutes against an app that was still starting up, and P1's first section fails on that cold auto-launch) and T756 (`tab-strip.ps1`'s T204 close-click arm went red once on a correct build and passed on the next run).

- 2026-08-11: T539 - a bare file path in a pane banner is a LINK now, so the user's `D:\...\file.mp4` opens Explorer with the file selected instead of doing nothing. T165 had already built the click side (a path-shaped target is a `.file`, a plain click reveals, Copy Path in the menu); what was missing was that nothing ever HANDED it a path - win32 banner markdown had no autolink pass at all, so only `[label](target)` became a link and a pasted path was inert text. `banner_markdown` gains that pass, Mac's `SurfacePaneBanner.autolink` ported rule for rule (scheme-only URL matching, the word-boundary test, trailing punctuation shed with the balanced-bracket exception, nothing inside a code span or an explicit link's label) with the spellings that are native here added: a drive path (`D:\`, `D:/`), a UNC share (`\\server\share\...`), and the backslash form of `~`, `.` and `..`. Two Windows-shaped details carry the change. The pass runs FIRST in the inline loop, ahead of the backslash-escape branch, because a UNC path opens with the escape character itself - `\\server\share` was otherwise eaten one `\` at a time and rendered `\servershare`; a `\` that does not open a UNC path still falls through, so `\*` escapes exactly as before. And resolution is parse-time against a new `PathContext` (`cwd` from `surface.pwd`, `home` from `homedir.home`) because the parser is what decides whether `.\out\a.mp4` is a link at all: with nothing to resolve against it stays plain text rather than becoming a link that goes nowhere, which is Mac's rule for the same field. `joinPath` collapses `.`/`..` itself rather than calling `std.fs.path.resolveWindows`, which falls back to the PROCESS cwd when its base is not absolute - a banner must never point at the app's launch directory. 8 new unit tests in the none lane, plus the one existing expectation this legitimately changes (an escaped `\[x](https://y.io)` now yields three runs, because the URL left sitting in parens is a bare URL and autolinks on its own - Mac splits it the same way). New section 6j in `test\win32\pane-banner.ps1` (ALL PASS, 110): the right-click menu over the bare path is a FILE menu leading with Reveal in File Explorer, Ctrl+click opens a viewer pane whose `url` is the whole path backslashes and all, and the same path minus its drive prefix opens NO menu at the same pixel. That section started as a link-colored-pixel count and was rewritten: ClearType fringes put blue-dominant pixels on the edge of every glyph, so plain text scored 393 "link" px against a real link's 2413 and no threshold separated them - the menu is binary and needs no constant. Floor: none/win32/agent PASS, P1-P3 ALL PASS.

- 2026-08-11: T538 - a terminal split off a browser pane now opens where THAT WINDOW is working, instead of in another window's folder or in home. The fallback was never a window answer: a viewer with no file contributes no cwd (correctly - `splitWorkingDirectory` is a file rule), and what answered instead was the core's `apprt/surface.zig` `newConfig` plus `Surface.init`'s T185 live-pwd override, both of which read `app.focusedSurface` - an app-GLOBAL value. So the new pane inherited from whichever window last held focus, or, with nothing focused, from the shell's home default. That is also why it read as flaky: the same sequence run in isolation PASSED, because there the focused pane happened to be in the window being split. New pure `SplitTree.nearestLeaf` (`src/datastruct/split_tree.zig`, 3 tests in the none lane) finds the leaf nearest a given one, entering each sibling subtree from the side FACING it - the pane the viewer shares a divider with, which is almost always the pane it was split off. `Window.viewerSplitFallbackCwd` uses it: the focused surface when it belongs to this window (the ordinary case, unchanged, and what macOS does), else the nearest terminal pane in the viewer's own tab, read by T185's live-pwd rule so a cmd.exe that reports no pwd still gives its real directory. The value rides the existing `viewer_cwd` seam, so the exec baton and the agent OPEN both inherit it - verified by hand on a live instance with session-persistence ON, with the focus both in-window and parked in a second window. `viewer-panes.ps1` gained a cross-window arm that parks the focus next door first, so the old assertion cannot pass by luck again; ALL PASS (185) x3, and teeth-checked by stubbing the fallback to null and rebuilding, where the run reports 3 FAILURE(S) with the cross-window one naming the far window's folder. That measurement also refutes T749's diagnosis (which blamed T506's launch-cwd default for the same failing assertion): the wrong value tracked the FOCUSED WINDOW, not the script's cwd, so T506 needs no precedence change - T749 is closed as a duplicate of this. Floor: none/win32/agent PASS, P1-P3 ALL PASS. Filed T759 (the Mac half - `splitConfigFromViewer`'s nil-file leg has the same app-global hole) and T760 (a non-persistent terminal split inherits the focused surface rather than the pane it was split off, so the exec and agent backends disagree about what a split inherits).

- 2026-08-11: T723 - if the background agent stops answering and never comes back, the app keeps trying instead of leaving your panes dead. The unknown the task was filed on is now answered by measurement, and the answer was the worst one: the abort was TERMINAL. `Connection.withLink` fires the link observer only on a real state CHANGE, and the only transition left out of `reconnecting` is to `dead`, which `LinkState` reaches solely via `onSessionGone` - a server-sent DETACHED frame that a wedged or killed agent never sends. So no second down edge ever arrived, `beginAgentSettleWatch` was never re-armed, and nothing re-dialed; the panes stayed frozen until the user quit, which is the exact failure in-place recovery exists to remove. An abort now arms a bounded, backed-off retry - policy pure in `agent_recovery.zig` (`retry_delays_ms` 2/4/8/15/30/30s, `retryDelayMs`, `evaluateRetry`), mechanism in `App.armAgentRecoveryRetry`/`tickAgentRecoveryRetry` on a one-shot timer, armed at the single re-dial-failure site so every caller of recovery inherits it. It stands down the moment the old link heals on its own, because the abort left the panes riding that connection (recovery retires one only when the re-dial SUCCEEDS) and rebuilding over a heal would replace working panes. When the schedule is spent the app says so in the pane, as a give-up banner naming the state and the remedy, and a pane already carrying a banner keeps it (T422's rule); the notice is cleared BEFORE the next capture, since the rebuild restores banners FROM the capture and would otherwise re-apply "your shell is frozen" to the pane that just came back. New sections I and J in `test\win32\agent-recovery.ps1` (ALL PASS, 76): I holds the wedge past the re-dial and then KILLS the frozen agent - no healed link to fall back on, so only the retry can answer - and J is the softer resume arm the task named. Teeth-checked by compiling the arming out, where I goes 5 red including the typed-marker liveness oracle while the app-pid and topology arms still pass, which is why neither can be the oracle. One harness lesson worth keeping: the two arms must run kill-first, because a wedge held past `single_instance.heartbeat_stale_after_ms` (45s) lets the app's own spawned challenger take the stale guard and recovery then succeeds on its first try - an arm that inherits an already-frozen agent never reaches the abort under test, which is how the second arm first failed. Floor: none/win32/agent PASS, P1-P3 ALL PASS. Filed T763 (the Mac half - it has a short ladder inside the re-dial plus a background `warmUp`, and whether that covers a longer wedge is unmeasured) and T764 (a pane opened DURING a wedge is handed the stuck shared connection instead of the documented exec fallback, because `sharedConnection`'s fast path only rejects `.dead`).

- 2026-08-11: T515 - a `+split` that runs a command now opens where the pane it split is, not where the window you last clicked in is. The task was filed against the wrong mechanism, and recording that is half the value: T144's `termio.Remote.openWorkingDirectory` already falls back to the surface config's cwd for the LOCAL agent, so the null `working_directory` in the explicit-command override never actually reached the agent as "no cwd". What answered instead was the CORE's inheritance, which is app-GLOBAL (`apprt/surface.zig` `newConfig` reads `app.focusedSurface`) - the same seam T538 fixed one layer over. With the split parent focused it gives the right answer for the wrong reason, which is why every same-window test of this passed for months; park the focus in a second window and the new pane opens in THAT window's directory. A cross-machine window has it worse still, since a local path is deliberately withheld from a remote agent and there is no fallback at all. `IpcHandlers.handleSplit` now resolves the split PARENT's live cwd whenever it builds an override and no `--working-directory` was passed, through a new shared `Window.inheritedCwd` - the one GET_CWD site, which `buildRemoteInherit` was refactored onto so the two paths cannot drift. An explicit `--working-directory` still wins; a split with nothing explicit still breaks to a null baton and inherits as before. `test\win32\local-split-no-command-rerun.ps1` gained sections 4b/5/6 (ALL PASS, 27): the explicit-command split keeps its parent's cwd, an explicit path beats it, and the cross-window arm - the one with teeth - parks focus in a far window first. Teeth-checked by reverting the local-agent half and rebuilding, where that arm reports the far window's directory and goes 2 red while sections 4 and 5 still pass, which is exactly the masking that hid this. Floor: none/win32/agent PASS, P1-P3 ALL PASS. Filed T761 (the Mac's own gap, found while checking its behavior: `BaseTerminalController.newSplit` gates inheritance on `remoteWorkingDirectory` while the IPC handler writes `workingDirectory`, so an explicit `+split --working-directory` looks dropped on an agent-backed window); the exec leg of this same rule is already T760, and T762 was filed for it before that was noticed and closed as its duplicate.

- 2026-08-11: T263 - the test harness can press a title-bar button now, so a click there stops silently doing nothing. `Send-TestMouse` posted client mouse messages at every point; since T254 the caption band is client PIXELS the window claims back through `WM_NCHITTEST`, so Windows delivers `WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN` there and a posted `WM_LBUTTONDOWN` reaches no handler at all - a state indistinguishable from a broken button, which cost T260 seventeen assertions against a caption whose pixels and hit tests were both correct. `MouseEvent` now makes the decision `DefWindowProc`'s input path makes: ask the target `WM_NCHITTEST`, and deliver the `WM_NC*` family (code in wparam, SCREEN point in lparam, always the DBLCLK form for a double since `CS_DBLCLKS` governs client double-clicks only) whenever the answer is not `HTCLIENT`. `HTNOWHERE`/`HTTRANSPARENT`/`HTERROR` are deliberately NOT converted - all three mean "not me", which is the z-order question this harness does not ask, and the surface child answers `HTTRANSPARENT` over the split-divider grab band. A window that does not answer in 1.5s is treated as `HTCLIENT`, because a routing question must never hang a click. `-Client` forces the old path for a test whose subject IS it, `GHOZTTY_TEST_MOUSE_CLIENT=1` reproduces the pre-T263 harness from the same tree, and `Get-TestMouseRoute` exposes the decision so a script can assert "this point is the minimize button" before clicking and read a moved button as a moved button. `menu-bar.ps1`'s `Click-MenuHost` and `caption-bar.ps1`'s `ClickCaption` collapse back to ordinary clicks (the latter now takes two POINTS, so press-then-slide-off is a real gesture; `CaptionGeom` re-derives the button centers per window off the CLIENT origin, or the maximized restore click aims at the sky). New `test\win32\mouse-nc-routing.ps1` ALL PASS (14): the decision at three points, a plain click iconifying, `-Client` at the same point doing nothing as an on-demand reproduction of the bug, the negative control that an empty-band click presses nothing and leaves the app clickable, and the client path still taking focus; `-NegativeControl` fails as required. Regression sweep of every mouse-driven script ALL PASS (tab-strip 65, chrome-merged-row 28, tab-color 17, context-menu 42, dark-menus 10, focus-follows-mouse 14, focus-defer 17, keybinds-t01 31, hero-mode 68, chooser-menu 57, activity-monitor 115, host-settings 65). The one thing it cost: two `tab-strip.ps1` probes aim at the window's last pixel column to prove the STRIP does not claim it, and in the merged row that column is the caption's close button - a routed click there really closes the window, so both pass `-Client` and the first gained a route assertion that is a stronger statement about the inset than "clicking it did nothing". Floor: none/win32/agent PASS, P1-P3 ALL PASS, the three harness audits ALL PASS. Filed T767 (`tab-strip-autohide.ps1` derives its caption hit-test points with the pre-T496 button arithmetic, so its "..." probe lands on minimize and the script is red against a correct build - it contains no mouse call at all, so this was already there) and T768 (`persistence-flag.ps1` is red with four undeclared launches in `agent-attach-refused.ps1` and `url-scheme.ps1`, the same shape as T744).

- 2026-08-11: T264 - `caption-bar.ps1`'s private copy of the caption run's four x's now has to AGREE with `lib\ChromeGeometry.ps1` out loud, every run. The task offered two ways out of the duplicate and the answer was the less obvious one: KEEP the restatement. Section 2 measures PAINTED pixels against `CaptionGeom`'s numbers, so sourcing them from the module would move the probe points along with any drift and keep passing - the derivation would stop being checked by anything, in the one script whose job is checking it against reality. Option 1's "keep one assertion that restates the arithmetic" is the same duplicate wearing a smaller hat and would only cover one rect of four. New section 2b compares all four (`CaptionCloseLeft`/`CaptionMaxLeft`/`CaptionMinLeft`/`CaptionOverflowLeft`) plus the band height against `$geo.M` - the metrics `CaptionGeom` itself read, so same call and same window rect, and a difference can only be the arithmetic. The reasoning lives in `CaptionGeom`'s header where the next reader meets it, as the task asked. `GHOZTTY_TEST_CAPTION_SKEW=<n>` is the teeth-check: it shifts the restatement by n px, which is the same observable state as the module drifting by n, and one px inside a 46 DIP slab still hit-tests, clicks and paints identically - so a skewed run goes red in 2b and nowhere else. `caption-bar.ps1` ALL PASS (32, was 27); `GHOZTTY_TEST_CAPTION_SKEW=1` gives exactly 4 FAILURE(S) (28 passed), every one of them a 2b assertion. Floor: none/win32/agent PASS, P1-P3 ALL PASS. The sweep for other copies of this datum found three more scripts: `tab-strip-autohide.ps1` is genuinely RED on this commit (1 FAILURE(S), 14 passed) because it still models the pre-T496 run - re-measured and folded into T767, which T263's turn had already filed, and the new T769 was closed as its duplicate rather than kept - and `close-glyph-white.ps1` + `mouse-nc-routing.ps1` restate `CaptionCloseLeft`/`CaptionMinLeft` correctly but uncompared, filed as T770.

- 2026-08-11: T268 - the terminal vanishing when you confirm the agent refresh is a JOB-OBJECT KILL, not a hang and not a crash, and that is now measured rather than hypothesised. The trail T229/T421/T426 built finally had something to say: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ghoztty\ghoztty.log` holds 8 `user confirmed destructive agent refresh` lines and 6 step trails, and NOT ONE of them completes - `agent restart: pid N terminate returned` and `terminated local agent pid` each have 0 occurrences in 425018 lines. The most recent trail (line 421595) reaches T426's job facts, `self_in_job=yes self_job_flags=0x2000 kill_on_close agent_in_job=yes SHARED_JOB=no`, and stops; three lines later the relaunch guard records `app pid 43076 ENDED during the agent refresh` and restarts it as pid 50572, which is the app running on this box right now. So the app dies inside `TerminateProcess(agent)` - and it dies because it is a MEMBER of the agent's own kill-on-close job while the agent OWNS that job's last handle. `pty_child.zig` creates exactly one process-global job with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` (0x2000, no breakaway bits), assigns every PTY child to it and holds the handle for the agent's whole life; killing the agent closes it, and the job takes every member down with no exception and no chance to log. Measured live from inside a pane rather than argued: a read-only probe from this session reports `in_job=True`, `LimitFlags = 0x2000` - byte-identical to the dying app's own line - over a member list of exactly 8 processes, the agent's three `cmd.exe` pane shells (`ppid` = `ghoztty-agent.exe`) plus their descendants. The app gets in because `upgrade-ghoztty-windows.ps1` relaunches it with a plain `Start-Process` from a pane descendant, and a child of a job member is auto-assigned. `SHARED_JOB=no` is correct and was never an exoneration: a process is not a member of a job it merely owns a handle to, so T426 measured the right thing and asked the wrong question (its own `yes` came from `agent-upgrade.ps1` arm H, the harness's app-owned jail - the opposite direction, which T426 really did remove). The control comes free from the same probe: `IsProcessInJob` answers False for both the live app (relaunched with `escape=breakaway`) and the live agent, so escaping the job is not a theory about what would help, it is the state the surviving process is already in - and it is why this always looked intermittent, why four repro shapes in T229 all passed (every one launched the app from a harness, i.e. outside the agent's job), and why "it worked when I tried it" was never evidence. Consequence worth naming: the confirm dialog's promised rebuild is not failing, it is unreachable - the trail stops before `in-place recovery: re-dialed` every time. No source changed this turn; the deliverables are the write-up in T268.md, T675 re-scoped from "identify who puts the app in a kill-on-close job" to "break out of it" and raised P2 -> P1 with the answer and a repro requirement (the app must be launched FROM a pane), a pointer added to T426 so its "cause established and removed" is read as one direction of two, and new T771 (the probe asks membership when ownership is what kills; the answerable proxy is whether OUR job contains the agent's own children). - 2026-08-11: T279 - text a script composes now reaches the ghoztty CLI byte-exact, and the loop's own relaunch stops destroying the prompt it is relaunching with. PowerShell 5.1 builds a native command line itself, and its builder is not the inverse of the CRT parser every C/C++/Zig program uses to read one back: measured here with a `GetCommandLineW` oracle, it wraps an argument in quotes only when whitespace appears at a position preceded by an EVEN number of `"` characters, and it copies an embedded `"` through unescaped. Both halves corrupt silently at exit 0. The live cost, found by this task: `upgrade-ghoztty-windows.ps1:905/917` and `watchdog-ghoztty-windows.ps1:120` passed `--command=claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --continue "read go.md and go"`, and ghoztty received `--command=claude ... --continue read` plus `go.md`, `and`, `go` as three stray positionals - so every relaunch after an upgrade or a freeze came up with no loop prompt, while the log printed the correct string. `go-loop-watchdog.ps1` had already met this and routed around it with a generated `.cmd` shim, naming the same symptom in a comment, so it was known at one site and unfixed at the other two. The fix is not an escaper, and that is a proof rather than a preference: escaping `"` as `\"` leaves the `"` in place, so it still counts toward PowerShell's parity while the CRT no longer treats it as structural, and for text whose first space is preceded by an ODD number of quotes - `"a quoted phrase" then more`, an ordinary title - PowerShell declines to wrap, the CRT splits at the spaces, and the structural open quote that would fix it flips the parity straight back. A candidate escaper was written and measured first; it passes 17 of 18 payloads with exactly that class failing. So `scripts\lib\NativeArgv.ps1` builds the command line to the CRT's own rules and hands it to CreateProcess through `ProcessStartInfo.Arguments`, which is total and fixes every flag of every verb at once - no `--title-file`/`--banner-file` pair was added, because the defect is in our PowerShell call sites rather than in the product and a CLI flag is a cross-platform obligation bought to work around one shell (D70 records the call). The converted sites are the two relaunches plus the one HELPER in each of `go-loop-exec.ps1` and `go-loop-watchdog.ps1`, so a call added to those scripts later is safe by default; `--keys-file` stays the transport for a prompt. Bonus: reaching CreateProcess directly captures a GUI-subsystem exe's stdout with no `2>&1` merge, so a stderr line can no longer land inside a `+list --json` those scripts parse (T663 for these callers). Acceptance `test\win32\cli-argv-fidelity.ps1`, ALL PASS at 35 assertions: the token quoter as a pure function, then three hazardous payloads and a safe one round-tripped through `+rename --title=` and `+set-banner` against a live debug instance and read back with `+list --json`, with the naive `& $exe "--flag=$text"` transport re-sending every payload as the negative control (it must arrive corrupted) and a safe payload that must survive both ways, so neither an always-red harness nor a set of payloads that were never at risk can produce a pass. Floor green: all three lanes, P1-P3, and the five harness sweeps.
